method_challenges.topic: Path-policy omission is not digest-bound omission
method_challenges.detail: A same-path omission can set EXPLICITLY_WITHHELD even when its recorded digest differs from the descriptor. Path-only policy association must remain identity-unresolved rather than establish that the requested historical digest was withheld.
method_challenges.analytic_counterexample: A descriptor p/hashA with no included/source/baseline match and an omission p/hashB reaches EXPLICITLY_WITHHELD. hashA and hashB are symbolic unequal hashes; no real omitted artifact was inspected.
method_challenges.required_disposition: Separate exact omitted-hash association from same-path policy with unknown/different digest; retain unresolved requested identity.
method_challenges.v3_resolution: V3 separates LOCATOR_EXPLICITLY_WITHHELD_HASH from WITHHELD_PATH_POLICY_HASH_UNRESOLVED and expressly denies establishing presence/withholding for the latter digest.

method_challenges.detail: Records merge by declared path and digest, excluding referring root/generation/location. A matching candidate in one context can dominate later contexts; exact disposition is sticky. Only three examples are retained.
method_challenges.analytic_counterexample: An identical short path/hash in R and AR may have an exact R candidate but no exact AR candidate. One aggregated locator entry is not proof for each occurrence.
method_challenges.required_disposition: Call categories candidate-locator associations, not per-occurrence resolution; retain explicit sample cap and context-coalescing limits.
method_challenges.v3_resolution: V3 labels path/hash locators as existing in at least one context, and records cross-context grouping plus the first-three-example cap. It remains a prioritized candidate inventory, not all possible associations or per-occurrence proof.

method_challenges.detail: Every parsed JSONL value starts with an empty pointer and no physical-line field, making identical document/pointer examples ambiguous across line records.
method_challenges.required_disposition: Carry physical JSONL line numbers into retained example contexts; full occurrence closure is still not established.
method_challenges.v3_resolution: V3 starts JSONL example pointers with a synthetic /jsonl-line/N ordinal and retains within-value pointer escapes. This is not a standalone RFC6901 pointer into the whole JSONL file; line splitting uses Python splitlines.

method_challenges.topic: Hash presence does not validate descriptor semantics
method_challenges.detail: Size, mode, generation, canonical identity, range bounds and role are not validated. Hash alias/source/baseline lookup precedes range-like classification; a range fragment can locate an entire different blob with the same bytes. A generic lines count alone need not mean a range.
method_challenges.required_disposition: No whole-file/range/generation correctness claim from these categories. Range-like is heuristic. Preserve this limitation alongside counts.
method_challenges.v3_resolution: V3 explicitly disclaims size/mode/range/generation semantics and acknowledges range-like hash aliasing. Generic lines-key heuristic qualification remains in the promised companion note.

method_challenges.topic: Baseline source I/O and computed CRLF candidates
method_challenges.detail: The writer spawns read-only Git commands and buffers public baseline blob bodies as data. Suffix-based CRLF candidate bytes are computed, not observed checkouts. Initial result lacks standalone script/input/baseline-tree bindings.
method_challenges.required_disposition: Bind exact script/index/omissions/raw-source manifest and baseline commit/tree; label computed CRLF bytes as synthetic candidates; disclose public Git blob reads and lack of source/runtime review.
method_challenges.v3_resolution: V3 adds script, three startup-input and baseline commit/tree bindings, blob-stream count/bytes and computed-versus-observed CRLF caveats. Its binding rereads happen after initial global parsing; external freeze must cover startup through output/readback.

method_challenges.topic: Trusted input envelope, not a hardened general reader
method_challenges.detail: Startup JSON reads use path APIs and no supplied pins, duplicate path rows can overwrite lookup entries, descriptor files are read wholly before indexed hash assertion, and no no-follow/ownership/resource cap or fsync/readback exists inside the helper. Exclusive output creation prevents ordinary overwrite but does not itself bind parent directories or output durability.
method_challenges.required_disposition: Restrict use to separately admitted, trusted frozen inputs with parent-owned bounds/identity checks; independently bind/read back output. Do not present the helper as safe for arbitrary untrusted indexes or as a general validation runner.
method_challenges.v3_resolution: V3 explicitly relies on an externally supplied stable frozen path/size envelope rather than a sandbox. Parent remains responsible for bounded source/index/omissions/manifest/path/type/hash checks and final exact output identity.

method_challenges.detail: Only included parseable JSON/JSONL dictionaries with string path and lowercase64hex sha256 are selected. Markdown, alternate descriptor keys, omitted bodies and semantic dependencies are outside the inventory. JSONL parse failure skips the entire file. Standard json.loads accepts nonfinite constants unless rejected; the duplicate-key hook is not applied to startup JSON.
method_challenges.required_disposition: Preserve parse failures and explicit descriptor-selection rules; avoid an RFC-strict parsing or complete-closure claim. Later report/output additions do not automatically become scanned inputs.
method_challenges.v3_resolution: Bound ASSEMBLY.md explicitly says Python json rather than RFC-strict, limits duplicate-key rejection to scanned documents, calls a generic lines key heuristic, retains sampled-context and startup-before-binding/cooperative-freeze caveats, and leaves109+31 unresolved candidates open.
